Now I've viewed all 16 reference images. Let me analyze my findings:

**Summary of visual comparisons:**

- **Anthracnose**: All references show fruit disease (black spots on bananas) — clearly not matching
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: All references show fruit tip/rot disease — clearly not matching
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Shows discrete brown spots with yellow halos on leaves — not matching whole-plant wilting
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Shows yellow/dark streaks and spots on leaf surfaces — not matching
- **Bunchy_Top**: PlantWild_10 showed whole-plant with clustered leaves at top and dried outer sheaths — visually closest in structure; other two were an unusable video frame and a presentation slide
- **Panama_Disease**: Shows progressive yellowing/browning of leaves, outer leaves dying first — matches the disease progression seen in the test image

**Decision:** The test image shows a whole banana plant with severely withered/dried outer leaf sheaths at the base, dark pseudostem discoloration, and still-green new growth at the top. This progressive wilting pattern — outer leaves collapsing while new growth persists — is the hallmark of **Panama Disease** (Fusarium wilt). The disease invades through roots, browns the pseudostem internally, and causes outer leaves to yellow and die first. The Bunchy Top reference was somewhat structurally similar, but the test image lacks the distinctive narrow, erect, tightly clustered "bunchy" leaves; instead the upper leaves look normally shaped and spread.
